definitions.gloss: reap what you sow, you get what you deserve
definitions.explanation: Suffering the consequences of one's own actions. Originally a Buddhist concept of karma.

examples.japanese: それは{自業自得|じごうじとく}としか{言|い}えない。
examples.english: I can only say you brought it on yourself.

examples.japanese: {嘘|うそ}をついた{結果|けっか}、{信用|しんよう}を{失|うしな}った。{自業自得|じごうじとく}だね。
examples.english: As a result of lying, you lost trust. You got what you deserved.

examples.japanese: {勉強|べんきょう}しなかったから{不合格|ふごうかく}になった。{自業自得|じごうじとく}だ。
examples.english: I didn't study, so I failed. I reaped what I sowed.

notes:
{自業自得|じごうじとく} is a Buddhist-origin {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} meaning "you reap what you sow." It expresses that one's fate is determined by one's own actions (karma).

WORD FORMATION:
{自|じ} (self) + {業|ごう} (deeds/karma) + {自|じ} (self) + {得|とく} (obtain) = one obtains the results of one's own deeds

USAGE:
- Often used when someone suffers consequences of their own bad choices
- Can sound harsh or judgmental when directed at others
- Used as a noun or as a predicate with だ

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {自業自得|じごうじとく}だ: You brought it on yourself
- {自業自得|じごうじとく}としか{言|い}えない: I can only say it's self-inflicted
- それは{自業自得|じごうじとく}だよ: That's your own doing

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {因果応報|いんがおうほう}: karmic retribution (more neutral)
- {身|み}から{出|で}た{錆|さび}: rust from one's own body (similar meaning)
- {蒔|ま}いた{種|たね}: reap what you sow (lit. seeds you planted)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Originates from Buddhist teachings on karma. Use carefully, as it can come across as unsympathetic or blaming.
